article.headline: Games To Watch: Louisville visits unbeaten Kosciusko; Tupelo opens district play
article.html:
Kosciusko has protected a perfect record through six games. Friday brings a different measure of that start: a home district meeting with Louisville, with both teams arriving 1-0 in league play. That matchup leads our October 9, 2026 Games To Watch selection, alongside unbeaten Tupelo’s district opener at Southaven. All five selected football games are scheduled for 7 p.m. CDT.

Louisville at Kosciusko: unbeaten start meets a district test

The Whippets enter 6-0, while the visiting Wildcats are 4-2. The overall records favor Kosciusko, but the district records put them on equal footing. Each already has a league victory; their meeting offers an early chance to separate from a fellow district winner. Kosciusko’s perfect start and Louisville’s opportunity to disrupt it give this game stakes beyond the overall standings.

Tupelo at Southaven: a perfect record enters league play

Tupelo takes a 6-0 record to Southaven, which enters 1-3. Both teams are 0-0 in district play, making this the point where the Golden Wave’s unbeaten start begins to carry league consequences. Southaven’s difficult overall start has yet to cost it a district game; Tupelo’s six victories have yet to give it a league advantage. Our previous Friday-night reporting provides more background on the Golden Wave’s season.

Germantown at Starkville: a district opener after a setback

Starkville enters 4-1 after a 38-31 loss to Brandon on September 25. The Yellowjackets now welcome a 3-2 Germantown team from Madison, with both teams starting district play at 0-0. Starkville’s first league test therefore doubles as an opportunity to respond to that defeat, while Germantown opens its district schedule against a host that has lost only once.

Non-district tests for Ripley and Walnut

Ripley travels to New Albany at 1-5, carrying a five-game losing streak that includes a 22-10 defeat to Clarksdale on October 2. The 3-2 Bulldogs give the Tigers another opponent with a winning record. This meeting is non-district: Ripley’s immediate task is to interrupt that slide, rather than change its league standing.

Walnut, meanwhile, hosts Biggersville after beating Ashland 36-14 on October 2. That victory left the Wildcats at 3-3 entering this non-district matchup against the 1-5 Lions. Walnut can build on a winning result at home, while Biggersville arrives looking to improve a difficult overall start.

These are scheduled starts; check school announcements for late changes before traveling. This selection covers football games whose date, kickoff and team information could be verified. Volleyball, cross country, swimming and golf were also checked, but no additional event met those verification requirements before publication.
